grh_529c6cd8224f3c8651a8.title: Shah-nama
paragraphs: Two trusted museum couriers carrying the priceless Persian Shah-nama back to Tehran arrange to steal it by cooperating with hijackers and a wealthy collector. Their plan turns violent when undercover Scotland Yard Inspector Fenton identifies the criminals and is killed after the aircraft is forced down and burned. A female Scotland Yard sergeant traveling under cover follows the thieves with the aircraft captain, while one of the young couriers begins to regret entering the scheme. At the collector's remote farmhouse the couriers themselves are betrayed and threatened with death, escape, and eventually join the pursuing officer and captain. The captain takes the collector's small plane, recovers the manuscript, radios authorities to arrest the collector and his daughter, and flies the Shah-nama back toward safety.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on June 29, 1979. It is listed as episode 105 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Fletcher Markle, Hans Conried, Lloyd Bochner, Lou Horne, and Richard Peel. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Alan Caillou as writer, and [[person|howard-duff|Howard Duff]] as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_52db36e95cda08156fcd.title: Nina Rosa
paragraphs: An American mining engineer travels to Peru to evaluate the Nina Rosa mine and falls in love with its beautiful heiress, Nina Rosa, provoking the powerful gaucho Pablo. grh_523097977b5257c93fd6.title: Words at War 43-11-09 (22) to All Hands
paragraphs: Lieutenant John Mason Brown dramatizes portions of his own To All Hands, recounting service aboard an American flagship during the amphibious invasion of Sicily. Assigned to the bridge, Brown broadcasts battle developments to sailors below decks who cannot see the action, describing the convoy, landings, air attacks and the anxious hours offshore. His farewell to the ship emphasizes the shared hardships and fellowship created by the campaign, comparing the crew's bond to Shakespeare's band of brothers after a common day of battle.
